newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-HudCon hopes for higher profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-HudCon hopes for higher profit.

text.p: Property investment group Hudson Conway Ltd hopes to achieve a higher profit in the current year ending June 30, although the property market remains flat, chief executive Lloyd Williams said on Monday.
Asked if the company was confident of a higher profit in the current year, Williams told reporters: "We hope so. But I wouldn't say the property markets are improving."
Hudson Conway, which had about A$140 million invested in property at June 30, reported a net profit of A$25.7 million for 1995/96, about level with its 1994/95 after-tax earnings.
Williams suggested that if the current year's net profit rose, the increase would be marginal.
"We would hope that we were going to edge up as you would say," he told Reuters later.
Australia's low inflation rate meant the group needed to create new assets or add value to existing assets to maximise returns on its property portfolio, Williams said.
"We have projects in hand that are going forweard at all times," he said.
Earlier, chairman Sir Roderick Carnegie told the company's annual meeting here that Hudson was tendering as part of a syndicate for the privatisation of Melbourne airport.
It is also bidding to develop Melbourne's 220-hectare docklands site, near the city centre.
